A bill for an act relating to transportation; amending driver's license suspension requirements for criminal vehicular operation and criminal vehicular homicide offenses; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 171.187, subdivisions 1, 3; 629.344.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 171.187, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Suspension required.
The commissioner shall suspend the driver's license of a person:
(1) for whom a peace officer has made the certification described in section 629.344 that probable cause exists to believe that the person violated section 609.2112, subdivision 1, paragraph (a)[-, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6)-]; 609.2113, subdivision 1, [-clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); subdivision 2, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or subdivision-][+ 2, or+] 3, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or 609.2114, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), [-clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6), or subdivision 2, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6)-][+ or 2+]; or
(2) who has been formally charged with a violation of section 609.20, 609.205, 609.2112, 609.2113, or 609.2114, resulting from the operation of a motor vehicle.

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective August 1, 2025, and applies to certifications made on or after that date. +]

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 171.187, subdivision 3, is amended to read:

Subd. 3.
Credit.
If a person whose driver's license was suspended under subdivision 1 is later convicted of the underlying offense that resulted in the suspension and the commissioner revokes the person's license, the commissioner shall credit the time accrued under the suspension period toward the revocation period imposed under section 171.17, subdivision 4, or for violations of section 609.20[-,-][+ or+] 609.205[-, or 609.2112, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), clause (1), (7), or (8); 609.2113, subdivision 1, clause (1), (7), or (8); subdivision 2, clause (1), (7), or (8); or subdivision 3, clause (1), (7), or (8); or 609.2114, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), clause (1), (7), or (8), or subdivision 2, clause (1), (7), or (8)-].

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective August 1, 2025. +]

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 629.344, is amended to read:

629.344 CRIMINAL VEHICULAR OPERATION AND MANSLAUGHTER; CERTIFICATION OF PROBABLE CAUSE BY PEACE OFFICER.
If a peace officer determines that probable cause exists to believe that a person has violated section 609.2112, subdivision 1, paragraph (a)[-, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6)-]; 609.2113, subdivision 1, [-clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); subdivision 2, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or subdivision-][+ 2, or+] 3, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or 609.2114, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), [-clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or subdivision 2, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6)-][+ or 2+], the officer shall certify this determination and notify the commissioner of public safety.

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective August 1, 2025, and applies to determinations made by a peace officer that probable cause exists made on or after that date. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to transportation; amending driver's license suspension requirements for criminal vehicular operation and criminal vehicular homicide offenses; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 171.187, subdivisions 1, 3; 629.344.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 171.187, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Suspension required.
The commissioner shall suspend the driver's license of a person:
(1) for whom a peace officer has made the certification described in section 629.344 that probable cause exists to believe that the person violated section 609.2112, subdivision 1, paragraph (a); 609.2113, subdivision 1, 2, or 3, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or 609.2114, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), or 2; or
(2) who has been formally charged with a violation of section 609.20, 609.205, 609.2112, 609.2113, or 609.2114, resulting from the operation of a motor vehicle.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2025, and applies to certifications made on or after that date.

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 171.187, subdivision 3, is amended to read:

Subd. 3.
Credit.
If a person whose driver's license was suspended under subdivision 1 is later convicted of the underlying offense that resulted in the suspension and the commissioner revokes the person's license, the commissioner shall credit the time accrued under the suspension period toward the revocation period imposed under section 171.17, subdivision 4, or for violations of section 609.20 or 609.205.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2025.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 629.344, is amended to read:

629.344 CRIMINAL VEHICULAR OPERATION AND MANSLAUGHTER; CERTIFICATION OF PROBABLE CAUSE BY PEACE OFFICER.
If a peace officer determines that probable cause exists to believe that a person has violated section 609.2112, subdivision 1, paragraph (a); 609.2113, subdivision 1, 2, or 3, clause (2), (3), (4), (5), or (6); or 609.2114, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), or 2, the officer shall certify this determination and notify the commissioner of public safety.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2025, and applies to determinations made by a peace officer that probable cause exists made on or after that date.
